summary: Postinstall credential stealer exfiltrates cloud, AI, and developer secrets to Telegram and a bare-IP endpoint
details: On npm install, the package's postinstall hook runs index.js, which first aborts if it detects a CI or sandbox environment (NODE_ENV=test, CI=true, JEST_WORKER_ID, VITEST, or /.dockerenv) and otherwise sleeps a random 5-15 seconds before harvesting. It then reads canonical installer-secret paths — SSH private keys under ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.kube, ~/.npmrc, ~/.gitconfig and ~/.git-credentials, ~/.docker, ~/.netrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.cargo, gh hosts, and vercel/netlify/supabase/firebase tokens — and enumerates process.env for variables matching credential keyword patterns (TOKEN/KEY/SECRET/etc.). The collected host, user, cwd, node version, credential files, and environment variables are JSON-serialized, base64-encoded, and POSTed to two hardcoded destinations: the Telegram Bot API (api.telegram.org sendDocument to bot 8797336493 / chat 8814152665) and a plaintext HTTP endpoint at http://2.26.82.63:8888/collect. The 999.0.0 version and package-name shape are consistent with a dependency-confusion lure.
